summary: Director John Landis's reckless pursuit of realism on the 1982 Twilight Zone movie, with illegally hired child actors, explosions and a low helicopter, killed Vic Morrow and two children; he was later acquitted of manslaughter.

evidence.note: Landis biography begins with his 1950 Chicago birth and LA upbringing
Warner Bros reboot; Landis and Spielberg produce the anthology film in 1982
night shoot with children breaks child labor law; crew objections overruled
pilot and camera operator raise safety fears that are passed over
fatal scene filmed at Indian Dunes Park on the Santa Clara River, California
detailed account of the crash killing Morrow and the two children
Warner Bros lawyers argue the six-year-old assumed the risk; suits settled
grand jury indicts Landis, Folsey and Allingham for manslaughter
jury acquits the defendants; trial ran about three years after the crash
segment on Spielberg's role as producer and avoidance of testimony
coda on son Max Landis and the 2017 abuse accusations against him

notes: Main span ends 1987 (acquittal) from general knowledge; transcript only says the case took about three years. Covered span runs to 2022 because of the lifetime rule for living primary subject Landis. Exorcist/Hitchcock material is background comparison and not counted. Policing-incarceration used for the criminal trial for lack of a courts/justice theme; no theme for workplace or film-set safety, so labor-exploitation stands in.
